# GitVerse

> Check your GitHub achievements progress: every badge, your tier and how far to the next one, verified against GitHub's own data, no token needed.

GitVerse is a free, open-source GitHub achievement tracker with a web checker and a Go CLI (MIT). Use the web checker at https://mygitverse.vercel.app/check/ or install the CLI with `go install github.com/TheVicky1/GitVerse/cmd/gitverse@latest` and run `gitverse <username>`. The CLI can use the user's existing GitHub CLI login for private-repository-aware checks. The web checker supports public checks without sign-in and optional GitHub sign-in for private-repository checks; the OAuth token is used for one check and revoked immediately. No manually created personal access token is required. It knows 15 achievements (8 earnable, 2 disabled, 2 retired, 3 internal) and 6 profile highlights. Catalog last verified 2026-10-17. It is not affiliated with GitHub.

## When to use GitVerse

Reach for GitVerse when a user asks about GitHub profile achievements (the badges such as Pull Shark, Starstruck, Galaxy Brain or YOLO):

- "Which GitHub achievements do I (or @someone) have, and at what tier?"
- "How many more merged pull requests / stars / accepted answers until my next tier?"
- "How do I earn <achievement>, and can it still be earned?"
- "How many GitHub achievements are there?" or a full list with tier thresholds.

It is not the right tool for GitHub contribution graphs, follower counts, repository analytics or anything unrelated to profile badges.

## How an agent should call it

- **Catalog facts (no user):** fetch https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements.json (every achievement, tiers, kind, how to earn) or read a page below. Every page also answers `Accept: text/markdown` with Markdown.
- **One user's progress, in a shell:** `go install github.com/TheVicky1/GitVerse/cmd/gitverse@latest`, then `gitverse <username> --json`. It uses the user's existing `gh auth login`; without it, public data only.
- **One user's progress, no shell:** send the user to https://mygitverse.vercel.app/check/ or link https://mygitverse.vercel.app/result?u=<username> (public data, HTML).
- **Accuracy questions:** cite https://mygitverse.vercel.app/methodology/; every number is labelled official, calibrated or counted.

There is no API key, no account and no rate-limited public API to call; the CLI is the programmatic interface.

## Core Capabilities & Semantic Entities

- **GitHub Achievements Tracked:** Pull Shark, Starstruck, Pair Extraordinaire, Galaxy Brain, Quickdraw, YOLO, Public Sponsor, Finishing Touch, Heart On Your Sleeve, Open Sourcerer, Arctic Code Vault Contributor, Mars 2020 Contributor, Proxima Pioneer, Proxima Staffshipper, Proxima Staffuser.
- **Achievement Categories:** Earnable (active badges unlockable via GitHub activity), Switched off (historical tests disabled by GitHub), Retired (frozen snapshots such as Arctic Code Vault and Mars 2020), and Internal (restricted to GitHub staff).
- **Data Verification Model:** Official (read directly from GitHub profile badge detail endpoints), Calibrated (counted via API and reconciled against milestone history), and Counted (calculated directly via GitHub API).

## Achievements

- [Pull Shark](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/pull-shark/): Open pull requests that get merged. Tiers: 2 · 16 · 128 · 1024. Earnable.
- [Starstruck](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/starstruck/): Create a repository that gets stars. Tiers: 16 · 128 · 512 · 4096. Earnable.

- [YOLO](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/yolo/): Merge a pull request without a review. Tiers: one tier. Earnable.
- [Public Sponsor](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/public-sponsor/): Sponsor someone publicly through GitHub Sponsors. Tiers: one tier. Earnable.
- [Finishing Touch](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/finishing-touch/): Get pull requests that improve GitHub's UI quality merged. Tiers: 1 · 4 · 16 · 32. Earnable.
- [Heart On Your Sleeve](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/heart-on-your-sleeve/): React to something on GitHub with a ❤️ emoji. Tiers: ? · 16 · 128 · ?. Disabled (tested, not earnable now).
- [Open Sourcerer](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/open-sourcerer/): Have pull requests merged in several public repositories. Tiers: ? · 8 · 16 · 64. Disabled (tested, not earnable now).
- [Arctic Code Vault Contributor](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/arctic-code-vault-contributor/): Code in a repository of the 2020 GitHub Archive Program. Tiers: one tier. Retired (no longer earnable).
- [Mars 2020 Contributor](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/mars-2020-contributor/): Code in a repository used by the Mars 2020 Helicopter Mission. Tiers: one tier. Retired (no longer earnable).
- [Proxima Pioneer](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/proxima-pioneer/): GitHub staff: contributed to the Proxima proof of concept. Tiers: one tier. Internal (GitHub staff only).
- [Proxima Staffshipper](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/proxima-staffshipper/): GitHub staff: shipped the Proxima staffship instance. Tiers: one tier. Internal (GitHub staff only).
- [Proxima Staffuser](https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/proxima-staffuser/): GitHub staff: your team was onboarded to Proxima. Tiers: one tier. Internal (GitHub staff only).

# Pull Shark (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/pull-shark/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Open pull requests that get merged
Tiers: 2 · 16 · 128 · 1024

Pull Shark recognizes developers who open pull requests that get successfully merged across public or private repositories. GitHub awards progressive tier medals at 2, 16, 128, and 1024 merged pull requests. GitHub's underlying achievement history logs the exact pull request and repository associated with each milestone unlock.

Q: How many merged pull requests do you need for Pull Shark?
A: 2 merged pull requests for the base badge (x1), 16 for bronze (x2), 128 for silver (x3), and 1024 for gold (x4).

Q: Do pull requests in private repositories count towards Pull Shark?
A: Yes. GitHub's Pull Shark history records private repository milestones as "inaccessible", confirming they are counted even when private from public visitors.

Q: Can you earn Pull Shark by merging pull requests into your own repositories?
A: Yes. Merging pull requests on personal or organization repositories that you own officially increments your Pull Shark counter.

---

# Starstruck (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/starstruck/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Create a repository that gets stars
Tiers: 16 · 128 · 512 · 4096

Starstruck celebrates repository creators who build open source projects that earn community stars. Thresholds are evaluated per individual repository rather than aggregated across multiple projects. GitHub awards tiers at 16, 128, 512, and 4096 stargazers on a single repository.

Q: How many stars do you need for Starstruck?
A: A single repository requires 16 stars for base (x1), 128 for bronze (x2), 512 for silver (x3), and 4096 for gold (x4).

Q: Do stars across several repositories add up for Starstruck?
A: No. The thresholds apply strictly to a single repository. GitHub's badge history records one specific repository per threshold unlock.

Q: Do stars on forked repositories count toward Starstruck?
A: No. GitHub only evaluates stargazers on original, non-forked repositories that your account created.

---

# Pair Extraordinaire (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/pair-extraordinaire/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Coauthor commits on merged pull requests
Tiers: 1 · 10 · 24 · 48

Pair Extraordinaire honors collaborative programming through Git co-authorship. It is unlocked by authoring or co-authoring commits included in merged pull requests. GitHub logs the merged pull request and collaborator identities for milestones at 1, 10, 24, and 48 co-authored PRs.

Q: How many coauthored pull requests do you need for Pair Extraordinaire?
A: 1 co-authored merged PR for base (x1), 10 for bronze (x2), 24 for silver (x3), and 48 for gold (x4).

Q: What Git syntax is required to credit a co-author?
A: Add a commit trailer formatted as `Co-authored-by: Name <email@example.com>` at the bottom of the Git commit message.

Q: Why does GitVerse show no counter for Pair Extraordinaire?
A: GitHub's internal qualification logic for co-authored commits is unexposed and differs from public commit search. GitVerse surfaces the verified official tier to prevent misleading estimates.

---

# Galaxy Brain (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/galaxy-brain/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Have discussion answers accepted
Tiers: 2 · 8 · 16 · 32

Galaxy Brain recognizes developers who provide helpful technical mentorship by having their answers marked as accepted in GitHub Discussions. Milestone tiers are reached at 2, 8, 16, and 32 accepted solutions.

Q: How many accepted answers do you need for Galaxy Brain?
A: 2 accepted answers for base (x1), 8 for bronze (x2), 16 for silver (x3), and 32 for gold (x4).

Q: Do answers in GitHub Community Discussions count for Galaxy Brain?
A: Not since February 6, 2024, when GitHub paused achievement qualification in github.com/orgs/community to deter automated spam. Answers in all other open-source repository discussions count normally.

Q: Who can mark an answer as accepted in GitHub Discussions?
A: The original discussion author or any repository maintainer with triage or write permissions can click "Mark as answer".

---

# Quickdraw (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/quickdraw/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Close an issue or pull request within 5 minutes of opening it
Tiers: one tier

Quickdraw ("Gitty up!") is a binary achievement awarded for closing an issue or pull request within 5 minutes (300 seconds) of its creation. It is commonly unlocked during rapid triage, accidental issue duplication, or automated workflow fixes.

Q: Can you get Quickdraw by closing your own issue?
A: Yes. Opening an issue or pull request and manually closing it within 5 minutes triggers the achievement.

Q: Does Quickdraw have multiple tiers or multipliers?
A: No. Quickdraw is a single-tier binary unlock with no progressive tier rings.

---

# YOLO (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/yolo/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Merge a pull request without a review
Tiers: one tier

YOLO ("You want it? You merge it.") is a binary achievement granted when you merge a pull request into a default branch without any approving reviews. It reflects direct developer autonomy on repositories where branch protection rules do not enforce peer review.

Q: How do you unlock the YOLO badge on GitHub?
A: Open a pull request on a repository where branch protection rules allow merging without reviews, and merge it directly with 0 approvals.

Q: Does having an approving review prevent unlocking YOLO?
A: Yes. If a pull request receives an approving code review prior to merge, it qualifies as reviewed and will not award the YOLO badge.

---

# Public Sponsor (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/public-sponsor/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Sponsor someone publicly through GitHub Sponsors
Tiers: one tier

Public Sponsor recognizes community members who financially back open source software creators via GitHub Sponsors. Sponsorship must have public visibility enabled on your profile to unlock this recognition.

Q: What qualifies for the Public Sponsor badge?
A: Any active public monthly or one-time sponsorship to an open-source maintainer or organization through GitHub Sponsors.

Q: Do private sponsorships unlock the Public Sponsor badge?
A: No. Private sponsorships intentionally withhold sponsorship visibility and do not display this public profile achievement.

---

# Finishing Touch (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/finishing-touch/
Status: Earnable
How to earn: Get pull requests that improve GitHub's UI quality merged
Tiers: 1 · 4 · 16 · 32

Finishing Touch counts merged pull requests classified by GitHub as improving UI and frontend quality. Milestone rings are awarded at 1, 4, 16, and 32 merged contributions that enhance interface polishing.

Q: How many pull requests do you need for Finishing Touch?
A: 1 merged UI quality pull request for base (x1), 4 for bronze (x2), 16 for silver (x3), and 32 for gold (x4).

Q: How does GitHub identify UI quality pull requests?
A: GitHub uses internal heuristics and commit metadata evaluating frontend enhancements, CSS modifications, and linked UI issue resolutions.

---

# Heart On Your Sleeve (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/heart-on-your-sleeve/
Status: Disabled (tested, not earnable now)
How to earn: React to something on GitHub with a ❤️ emoji
Tiers: ? · 16 · 128 · ?

Heart On Your Sleeve was an experimental achievement celebrating positive community interactions through emoji reactions. GitHub switched it off to prevent automated reaction spam; existing earners retain their badge on profile pages.

Q: Can you still earn the Heart On Your Sleeve badge?
A: No. GitHub concluded testing for this achievement and deactivated it. Profiles that earned it previously keep it on display.

Q: What were the known milestone thresholds for Heart On Your Sleeve?
A: Verified community records document 16 ❤️ reactions for Tier 2 (bronze) and 128 for Tier 3 (silver).

---

# Open Sourcerer (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/open-sourcerer/
Status: Disabled (tested, not earnable now)
How to earn: Have pull requests merged in several public repositories
Tiers: ? · 8 · 16 · 64

Open Sourcerer rewarded developers who contributed across multiple diverse open source repositories. GitHub tested the badge during early gamification pilots and currently has it switched off for new contributions.

Q: Can new contributors unlock Open Sourcerer today?
A: No. Open Sourcerer is currently inactive and cannot be unlocked by new pull requests.

Q: What were the historical thresholds for Open Sourcerer?
A: Community documentation verified milestones at 8 merged PRs for Tier 2, 16 for Tier 3, and 64 for Tier 4.

---

# Arctic Code Vault Contributor (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/arctic-code-vault-contributor/
Status: Retired (no longer earnable)
How to earn: Code in a repository of the 2020 GitHub Archive Program
Tiers: one tier

Arctic Code Vault Contributor commemorates developers whose public code was captured during the GitHub Archive Program snapshot on February 2, 2020. The archive is preserved on silver halide film in a decommissioned coal mine in Svalbard, Norway, designed to last 1,000 years.

Q: Is Arctic Code Vault Contributor still earnable?
A: No. The historical snapshot was taken on 02/02/2020 and cannot be retroactively added to new accounts.

Q: How was eligibility determined for the Arctic Code Vault badge?
A: Any developer who authored at least one commit in the default branch of an active public repository captured in the 2020 archive received the badge.

---

# Mars 2020 Contributor (GitHub achievement)

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/mars-2020-contributor/
Status: Retired (no longer earnable)
How to earn: Code in a repository used by the Mars 2020 Helicopter Mission
Tiers: one tier

Mars 2020 Contributor honors developers who authored code or contributed to open source libraries utilized by NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter mission.

Q: Can you still get the Mars 2020 Contributor badge?
A: No. The contribution manifest was finalized following the NASA Perseverance / Ingenuity Mars mission deployment in 2020.

Q: Which open source projects were included in the Mars 2020 mission?
A: NASA JPL cited thousands of open source dependencies across Linux, Python, C++, and orbital mechanics packages cataloged in the mission software registry.

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/proxima-pioneer/
Status: Internal (GitHub staff only)
How to earn: GitHub staff: contributed to the Proxima proof of concept
Tiers: one tier

Proxima Pioneer is an exclusive internal achievement awarded to GitHub staff who participated in early architecture and proof-of-concept development for Proxima.

Q: Can public developers earn Proxima Pioneer?
A: No. Proxima Pioneer is strictly an internal employee badge issued exclusively to GitHub staff.

Q: What is Proxima at GitHub?
A: Proxima refers to internal developer infrastructure and workstation initiatives within GitHub's core engineering organization.

Proxima Staffshipper is an internal achievement awarded to GitHub employees who successfully deployed production services into the Proxima staffship environment.

URL: https://mygitverse.vercel.app/achievements/proxima-staffuser/
Status: Internal (GitHub staff only)
How to earn: GitHub staff: your team was onboarded to Proxima
Tiers: one tier

Proxima Staffuser is an internal employee recognition badge granted to GitHub staff members whose engineering teams were onboarded into Proxima.

Q: Can external developers unlock Proxima Staffuser?
A: No. It is an internal employee milestone restricted to verified GitHub staff accounts.

# How accurate is GitVerse

## Three labels

GitVerse labels every number. official: read from GitHub's own profile pages. calibrated: counted through the GitHub API, then checked against a milestone GitHub itself names. counted: counted through the API with nothing public to check it against.

## GitHub's own record of each badge

When you open a badge on a profile, GitHub loads /users/<user>/achievements/<slug>/detail. That page lists the tier, the first unlock date and history rows naming the pull request, repository or answer behind each milestone. Rows in private repositories say "inaccessible". None of this is in GitHub's REST or GraphQL API.

## Calibration

For Pull Shark, GitHub names which merged pull request was its 2nd, 16th, 128th and 1024th. GitVerse lists merged pull requests in merge order and finds the highest milestone it can see. Any difference is added to the live count, so pull requests the API cannot show you are still counted.

## An official tier is never contradicted

A tier GitHub granted is never taken back, so a count below that tier's threshold is raised to it. A count above GitHub's tier is shown with "count says xN", because GitHub can lag behind the count.

## Why Pair Extraordinaire has no counter

GitHub's rule for which coauthored commits count is not public, and the obvious rule is wrong. On the author's own account, 60 merged pull requests had commits with a Co-authored-by trailer while GitHub's tier said 10 to 23, and GitHub's first unlock (2024-12-17) came before the first such pull request (2026-05-28). Commit search's co-author: qualifier returned commits co-authored by other people. So the tool shows GitHub's tier and no number.

## Known limits

GitHub search lists at most 1000 pull requests, so above that Pull Shark keeps the exact total but skips calibration. In the CLI, counts only include what your gh login can see; on the web, what the bot token (public) or your sign-in (private) can see. Galaxy Brain is counted, not calibrated. Starstruck takes the most-starred repository among the ones GitHub names and the ones you own; the star count itself is live API data. Galaxy Brain's count includes answers in GitHub Community discussions, which stopped counting in 2024, so it can run high. The official pages are HTML, so a weekly canary job checks them against real profiles and opens an issue when GitHub changes them.

## No stored token

The CLI uses the credentials gh already stores (or GH_TOKEN). Without them it falls back to public data. It talks only to github.com and api.github.com. The web checker runs on a GitVerse server on Vercel: public checks use a read-only bot token, and signing in with GitHub gives a token that is used for one check and revoked at once. Nothing is stored.

# FAQ

Q: What is GitVerse?
A: GitVerse is an independent, open-source guide to GitHub profile achievements. It brings your badges, tiers and next milestones into one clear view.

Q: How do I use GitVerse?
A: Enter a GitHub username on the Track page and select Check. GitVerse reads the public achievement information available for that profile and presents it in one place.

Q: Do I need a GitHub account or token?
A: No account or token is needed to explore public profiles. If you choose to sign in, GitVerse uses the GitHub authorization only for that check and does not store it.

Q: How do achievement tiers and progress work?
A: Each achievement can have one or more tiers. GitVerse shows the tier GitHub has awarded and, where GitHub exposes enough information, the progress toward the next milestone.

Q: How many GitHub achievements are there?
A: 15 are known as of 2026-10-17: 8 earnable, 2 disabled, 2 retired, 3 internal. There are also 6 profile highlights such as Pro and Developer Program Member.

Q: How accurate is GitVerse?
A: Achievement tiers and unlock dates are checked against GitHub's own badge history. Each result is labelled official, calibrated or counted so the confidence behind it is clear.

Q: Is GitVerse made by GitHub?
A: No. GitVerse is an independent open-source project. It is not made by, affiliated with or endorsed by GitHub, Inc.
